title: Control plane: retention policy schema + validation (data model, API contract, migrations, tests)
creator: Ethan Park
project: Enterprise Security & Compliance Foundation: Retention controls + compliance reporting pack
description:
Implement the v1 retention policy schema + validation in the control plane. This includes persistence (tables + migrations), API contract (read/write), and unit tests (schema validation + guardrails).

Context
- Retention controls are a top blocker in multiple enterprise security reviews. We need tenant-configurable retention with guardrails + auditable changes.
- This issue is limited to schema + validation + persistence. Effective-policy evaluation is tracked in ENG-2912.

References
- Confluence: Security & Compliance → Data residency & retention → “Retention policy schema and evaluation” (spec)
- Confluence ADR: “Retention enforcement strategy” (hybrid TTL + scheduled jobs; control plane owns source-of-truth policy)
- Design: DES-144 (Console UX will call these endpoints via ENG-2926)

Scope (in)
1) Data model (control plane)
- Persist retention policies per tenant.
- Support per-data-type retention durations and optional per-environment overrides.
- Support policy metadata fields necessary for auditability (created/updated, actor, source).
- Persist legal hold + exception flags in a way that enforcement and evaluation can consume deterministically.

2) API contract
- Read current policy (raw, not “effective”)
- Create/update policy (validated)
- Explicit “reset to default” action (so Console can revert from custom to defaults)
- Ensure all mutations emit an admin/audit event.

3) Validation + guardrails
- Enforce minimum and maximum retention by data type (server-side).
- Disallow “never delete” except where explicitly permitted by product (v1: generally disallowed).
- Prevent retention values that exceed backend capabilities for the selected deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) where we have hard limits.
- Validate environment scoping: only allow known env identifiers (prod/staging/dev) for Redwood-managed; allow explicit custom env labels for Private with allowlist.

4) Tests
- Unit tests for JSON schema parsing + validation.
- Golden test cases for edge conditions: missing fields, unknown data types, too short/too long durations, illegal holds conflict, etc.
- Migration tests (up/down) and backwards compatibility for existing tenants (no policy == default behavior).

Scope (out)
- Effective policy computation and precedence rules (ENG-2912)
- Backend enforcement jobs and datastore TTL work (ENG-2920 / ENG-2921)
- Console endpoints and UX (ENG-2926 / DES-144)

Acceptance criteria
- A tenant can store a retention policy and retrieve it via API.
- Invalid policies are rejected with actionable errors.
- Min/max retention guardrails are enforced server-side.
- Policy changes create an auditable admin event with actor + diff.
- Existing tenants without an explicit policy continue operating on defaults.
- Unit test coverage includes both “happy path” and guardrail failures.

Implementation notes (proposed)
- Introduce RetentionPolicy as an entity scoped to tenant_id.
- Store structured policy JSON plus normalized fields that we need for querying/audit (e.g., updated_at, updated_by_actor_id, source).
- Avoid deep normalization per data type in v1 to keep migrations low-risk; rely on schema validation + evaluation library for interpretation.
- Add an allowlisted enum of supported data types for v1 (e.g., audit_logs, admin_activity, request_metadata, telemetry_analytics, operational_logs_eligible).

Open questions
- Do we model min/max guardrails in config (feature flags) vs hardcoded constants? (proposal: config-driven so Security can update without redeploy)
- For Private: should we allow “unbounded” retention at policy level but warn it may not be enforceable? (proposal: disallow in API for v1; revisit once enforcement coverage is broader)

Rollout
- Feature-flagged at API layer: retention_policy_api_enabled
- Read endpoints can be enabled earlier than write endpoints.
- Limit write access to org admins + security admins via RBAC.

Notes for Compliance/Evidence
- Policy mutation events must be queryable for the compliance reporting pack (who changed retention, when, and what changed).
- Store a stable policy version hash for evidence snapshots (optional in v1, but recommended).

resolution: Implemented retention policy persistence + validation in the control plane with feature-flagged APIs, server-side guardrails, RBAC enforcement for mutations, audit events on change, and unit/migration tests. Defaults preserved for tenants without explicit policy.
